summary: Calculates image statistics such as average, min, max, count, or sum over full images, rows, columns, slices, or channel scopes.

key_params.name: op
key_params.note: Statistic operation: average, minimum, maximum, count, sum, minrgb, minrgba, maxrgb, or maxrgba

key_params.name: analyzechannel
key_params.note: Channel basis such as luminance, red, green, blue, alpha, rgbaverage, rgbmax, or independent

key_params.name: scope
key_params.note: Analyze image, rows, columns, or slices

key_params.name: mask
key_params.note: Optional mask channel: none, red, green, blue, alpha, or independent

common_gotchas: Minimum and maximum output the selected pixel values unless RGBA Independent-style analysis is used.
Exclude NaNs and Mask options add cost; leave them off unless bad pixels or masks are part of the design.
NaNs propagate through statistics unless excluded.
Use float pixel formats for Count Pixels and Sum to avoid precision loss.
key_concepts: Analyze TOP reduces TOP pixels into statistics such as average, minimum, maximum, count, and sum.
Scope controls whether the output is one value for the image, one value per row, one per column, or one per slice.
Minimum and maximum can return the RGBA value of the selected pixel rather than independent per-channel extrema.
TOP to CHOP is the intended bridge when the resulting statistic needs to drive channels or parameters.
Count Pixels and Sum should use float output precision for large images or high values.
The official TOP supports 3D textures and 2D texture arrays.
